thread.title: After the bell on Thursday, we received fiscal first quarter

author: Bill Maurer
title: After the bell on Thursday, we received fiscal first quarter
text:
After the bell on Thursday, we received fiscal first quarter results , for the company's holiday period, from technology giant Apple ( AAPL ). Going into the report, analysts were scrambling to cut estimates amidst rumors of iPhone X production cuts, which brought down shares from their recent all-time highs. As expected, the company beat for the holiday period but issued downbeat guidance for the current quarter. Overall though, the report was just fine.
Q1 results: 
If you didn't get a chance to read my earnings preview article, here it is again for you. I didn't provide any specific unit sales estimates, so I provided the chart below to show you were the street is on most things. However, just like most analysts, I thought the December quarter would be a pretty good one.
( Source: Philip Elmer-Dewitt's Earnings Smackdown ) 
When looking at the main results, basically all of the product categories came in light on unit sales, but average selling prices were really strong. Apple sold 77.3 million iPhones with an ASP of $796, which was almost $102 above the prior year period. The company also saw a $22 rise in iPad ASPs. Services revenue was a tad light, but that might have been due to analysts overestimating things a little after last quarter's huge surge on the one-time accounting adjustment. Other products revenues smashed estimates, likely on the heels of the Apple Watch.
In total, Apple came in at just under $88.3 billion in total revenues, beating the street by just over a billion dollars and the midpoint of its own forecast by nearly $3 billion. Gross margins came in at 38.4%, towards the top end of the company's range, while other income items also beat guidance like I noted in my preview article that they probably would. Overall, Apple came in at $3.89 for EPS, beating the street by three cents, and that includes the fact that a slightly higher than expected tax rate dinged EPS by almost a penny and a half.
